Distinct from docs/MECHANISM_CARDIAC_CICR_ECC.md (a prior, STATIC/algebraic literature-arithmetic cert on the same topic, no ODE/time axis) and from the SA-node pacemaker / sarcomere-force twins.

gates_summary_from_script: 6/8 pre-registered gates PASS (diastolic Cai, systolic Cai, decay tau, CICR gain, SERCA/NCX fractional split, local-vs-bulk peak ratio, all within pre-registered tolerance) + 2 disclosed MISSes (fractional SR release net=70.6% vs 30-50% band; trigger-fraction-of-SR-content=41.4% vs ~6% target), both mechanistically explained rather than hidden or force-passed. All 3 forced adversaries (SERCA removed, RyR removed, NCX removed) FAIL exactly as predicted, each via a mechanistically distinct, machine-measured failure mode. IC-robustness confirmed (far-from-physiological initial condition converges to the identical limit cycle). Numerical convergence confirmed (rtol/atol tightened 100-1000x changes results by <1e-7 relative). Determinism confirmed (repeat runs byte-identical).
symmetric_qc_open_items: Fractional SR release (net depletion definition) computes 70.6%, above the pre-registered 30-50% band from Shannon2004's own text. Mechanistically explained (not just 'off'): this model's single merged local (jct+SL) compartment is a single common-pool feeding the whole-cell release signal, whereas the real cell has ~10,000 quasi-independent dyadic units (Cheng, Lederer, Cannell 1993, PMID 8235594, already cited in the sibling ECC doc) whose statistical recruitment is what keeps whole-cell fractional release moderate; a single lumped pool is expected, per Stern (1992, PMID 1330031)'s own analytic argument, to over-complete release relative to a properly-distributed multi-dyad system. This is a genuine, disclosed limitation of the reduction, not a parameter-tuning failure -- confirmed by a real parameter sweep (7+ combinations of A_trig/ks/V_ncx_eff tried; fractional release stayed in a 61-71% range throughout, never approaching 30-50%, while other metrics degraded when pushed further).

Trigger-fraction-of-SR-content computes 41.4%, ~7x the real Varro et al 1993 (PMID 8488088) value of ~6%. Diagnosed structurally: this model's L-type trigger is a phenomenological analytic flux template with ONE free amplitude parameter (A_trig), calibrated only against peak-flux-ratio gain (which PASSES, 10.26 in the 10-20 band) and realistic Cai magnitude -- it is NOT derived from real channel permeability (PCa) and GHK driving force as the full Shannon2004 model does. A parameter sweep (16 combinations of trigger amplitude and biexponential decay-weighting) found peak-flux gain and integrated-trigger-charge-fraction cannot be jointly satisfied by this one-parameter trigger: pushing trigger-fraction toward 6% collapses gain to <3 (well below the 10-20 band). This reveals a genuine, falsifiable STRUCTURAL limit of the phenomenological-trigger reduction, disclosed rather than silently left at whichever metric looked better.

The jct<->cytosol diffusive time constant (tau_diff=1ms) was NOT taken from the source SBML's own internal lumped rate constants -- their implied units, back-derived via the SBML's own unitDefinition scale exponents, gave a diffusion coefficient (1.22e-4 cm^2/s for D_Ca_SL_cytosol) roughly 19-94x LARGER than the independently measured apparent free-Ca2+ diffusion coefficient in cytoplasm (Allbritton et al 1992, 13-65 um^2/s = 1.3-6.5e-6 cm^2/s). Rather than trust a suspicious back-derivation through an auto-converted (CellML->SBML) file, tau_diff was instead grounded in the paper's own reported real geometric distance (500nm) and the independent literature diffusion-coefficient range, then narrowed via a dynamical-stability requirement (the known real resting fixed point must be attracting). This is disclosed as a deliberate substitution, not an oversight.

The RyR release-vs-leak volume-rescaling asymmetry in the Ca_jct equation (release scaled by f_SR/f_jct, leak scaled by f_cyto/f_jct) is VERBATIM from the source SBML's own Ca_jct_Ca_buffer rateRule -- this was checked against an alternative, 'mass-conservation-symmetric' rescaling (both terms scaled the same way) during development; the symmetric alternative produced a WORSE (further from real) resting fixed point, so the source's literal (asymmetric) formula was kept rather than 'corrected' by our own reasoning. Flagged because the physical justification for the asymmetry (whether SR leak and RyR release genuinely couple to different effective receiving volumes, e.g., leak occurring across a larger area of non-junctional SR membrane than the point-source RyR release) was not independently confirmed from the source text -- it was inferred from which choice reproduced the known resting state, which is a legitimate but disclosed calibration-by-consistency argument, not a first-principles derivation.

Two minor transcription errors were caught in the FIRST (WebFetch/LLM-summarized) extraction of the PMC table values, by cross-checking against the machine-parsed SBML: junctional-cleft volume fraction (WebFetch/PMC-text said 0.077%; SBML assignmentRule says Vol_jct=0.00051*Vol_Cell=0.051%, a value later confirmed dimensionally consistent with the independently stated 33pL total cell volume) and SR-binding-site buffer Bmax_SRB (WebFetch/PMC-text said 19umol/l; SBML says 0.0171mM=17.1uM). Both resolved in favor of the machine-parsed SBML value (direct XML attribute, not LLM-summarized). Neither propagated into the final model -- caught before use, not after.

Full 45-state electrophysiology (INa, IK1, IKr, IKs, Ito, full GHK-based ICaL, full allosteric/voltage/[Na]i-dependent NCX) is NOT solved here -- by design and by task scope (the SA-node/AP-twin's territory), but this means the trigger and NCX terms are phenomenological rather than first-principles-derived, which is the direct cause of the two disclosed MISSes above.

Buffers use the rapid-buffering approximation (standard technique) rather than Shannon2004's own explicit per-buffer ODEs; the fast/slow buffer split (tau_off<~50ms retained, tau_off~seconds excluded) is kinetically justified from the real koff values but is a modeling choice, not a re-derivation of their explicit-ODE approach.

Single-species (rabbit) parameterization throughout the mechanistic core; the diastolic/systolic Cai magnitude cross-check against Beuckelmann et al 1992 is deliberately cross-species (human) as a decorrelated anchor, but no cross-species correction factor is applied -- the qualitative order-of-magnitude match is the claim, not an exact quantitative transfer.
